title: Sample 20-4: Pronunciation Key without Heading

illustrates.quote: (See Sample 20-4: Pronunciation Key without Heading on page 20-16.)

blocks.text:
a	add	o͝o	took	ə =
ā	ace	o͞o	pool	a in above
â	care	u	up	e in sicken
ä	palm	û	burn	i in possible
e	end	yo͞o	fuse	o in melon
ē	equal	oi	oil	u in circus
i	it	ou	pout
ī	ice	ng	ring
o	odd	th	thin
ō	open	th (crossed)	this
ô	order	zh	vision
blocks.features: Three-column pronunciation key with no heading; symbols in a sans-serif face, example words in a serif face; the schwa column is separated by rules and its example letters are in italics (above, sicken, possible, melon, circus); 'took' carries a breve-type mark and 'pool' a macron over the oo (the braille has @+ and @-)

print.notes: Print original is the picture on page 20-16 (gold-20-A/page-554.png); it is a key of 11 + 12 + 6 rows. The braille is on page 20-17 (page-555.png).
print.printFeatures: Pronunciation key arranged in three columns without a heading.

braille.notes: Two braille pages: lines 1-23 then, after the source's '-New Braille Page-' marker, page 2 lines 1-7 (pageBreaks index 23 = first line of page 2). Line-number field of 5 columns stripped (digit count of the largest number, 2, plus 3); the two footer lines and the marker are not braille; the 5 blank lines after the caption are the print picture area and are excluded. U+2800 cells converted to spaces.

uncertain: Line 1 is 43 characters in the source text (34 sevens, 6 spaces, '#,-') but the page image shows 34 solid cells, about 3 blank cells and 3 cells, i.e. 40 wide. Kept verbatim from the source; the gap in the source may be 3 cells too wide (a text-extraction fault).
The 'th (crossed)' and 'took'/'pool' print marks are read from a small image; the braille (@*<th>, @+<oo>, @-<oo>) is the authority.
resolution: braille.lines: both runs had faults. A left a form-feed character on line 1, listed the source's '-New Braille Page-' marker as a braille line (line 24) and recorded pageBreaks []; B kept the 4 blank picture-area lines (its pageBreaks [27] is consistent with that) and left a stray leading space on line 1. All other lines agree with the source in both runs. Re-derived from the source lines 16023-16053 by script: 30 lines, one page break at index 23. illustrates: A recorded rule '20.x' and the caption; B '20.8' with the contents line; the example is cited by the cross-reference sentence after 20.7.5, which is used. print: B empty ('TODO'); A listed the rows in one column and gave no italics/mark detail; rebuilt in the three-column layout from the image, same words. pdfPages: A empty; B [16, 17] agrees with the footers. Print description corrected 23 Sep 2026 (see printCorrections).

printCorrections.now: o͝o took (one breve over both o's, U+035D)
printCorrections.evidence: references/bana/braille-formats-2016.pdf p.554, rendered at 400 dpi and cropped to the "took" row: a single curved breve arc spans both o's. The gold features field already says "took carries a breve-type mark"; the text contradicted it. The braille uses @+<oo> (breve modifier) for took and @-<oo> (macron) for pool.

printCorrections.was: ōō pool / yōō fuse (two separate macrons)
printCorrections.now: o͞o pool / yo͞o fuse (one continuous double macron, U+035E)
printCorrections.evidence: same page: the macron is one unbroken line across both o's in "pool" and in "y-oo fuse"; braille groups them: @-<oo>, y@-<oo>. Not built by the runner (pronunciation key, not-representable), so no status effect.
